subject: food-technology
title: Spoilage: Yeasts, Moulds, Bacteria
welcome_lead: Why bread goes mouldy and milk turns sour.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: spoilage organisms and their conditions.
final_note: Spoilage tells you it's gone bad. Pathogens kill silently.

walkthroughs.body_html: Microbial growth requires F.A.T.T.O.M.: Food (nutrients), Acidity (pH 4.6-7), Temperature (5-63 °C), Time (≥4 hours), Oxygen (varies), Moisture (aw > 0.85 for most pathogens, > 0.6 for moulds).
Yeasts ferment sugars to alcohol and CO2 — useful for bread and beer; spoilage in fruit juice. Saccharomyces cerevisiae is bread/beer yeast.
Moulds tolerate low water activity — they grow on jam, dry bread, hard cheese. Some produce mycotoxins (aflatoxin from Aspergillus). Visible fluffy growth is the spore-bearing hypha.
